source_title: Anonymous family donates $50 million to expand access to lifesaving medicines
source_excerpt: An anonymous family from Connecticut has donated $50 million to Americares, a global health and disaster-relief organisation, in the largest gift in its history. Announced on September 9, 2026, the donation will help expand access to essential medicines, strengthen partnerships with healthcare providers and improve the long-term resilience of health systems. The family has supported the organisation for 30 years, and the contribution comes as cuts to international aid funding put pressure on healthcare programmes worldwide. The donation will be distributed over five years, with half earmarked for expanding healthcare access and the other half allocated to Americares' endowment to help sustain its work in the years ahead.How Americares plans to use the $50 million donationThe donation will support Americares' five-year strategy to improve access to healthcare, particularly in communities affected by poverty, disasters and fragile medical systems.According to the organisation's announcement, $25 million will support healthcare expansion, including its Access to Medicine programme. The remaining $25 million will strengthen its endowment, providing a stronger financial foundation for its long-term work.The healthcare component will help Americares expand medicine distribution, strengthen local healthcare partnerships and improve the reliability of medical supply chains. The organisation aims to ensure that patients and healthcare facilities can obtain essential treatments when they need them.The gift will also support Americares' goal of helping 100 million people access quality healthcare by 2030.Which countries and communities will benefit?Americares plans to expand its medicine-access work in high-need countries across sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East and North Africa, Asia, and Latin America. These regions include communities where fragile healthcare systems and persistent shortages of medicines can prevent patients from receiving appropriate treatment.The organisation also intends to increase support for safety-net health centres in the United States. These facilities provide healthcare to people who are uninsured or underinsured, and Americares plans to focus on states where policy changes are expected to increase the number of residents without health insurance.The donation is intended to strengthen existing healthcare networks rather than establish an entirely new system. By working with local providers, Americares aims to improve access to medicines and make healthcare delivery more reliable.Americares supports more than 4,000 health centres worldwideFounded in 1979, Americares is a US-based nonprofit that provides medicines, medical supplies, emergency assistance and health services to communities around the world.The organisation supports more than 4,000 health centres globally, working with local partners to improve access to treatment and strengthen healthcare systems. Its activities include distributing donated medicines, responding to natural disasters and humanitarian emergencies, and supporting long-term health programmes.In the year before the donation announcement, Americares delivered approximately $1.8 billion in aid. This included enough medicine to fill nine million prescriptions and three million medical supplies for patients in need, according to its September announcement.The organisation also responds to emergencies and helps communities restore essential health services after disasters. Its work spans both immediate humanitarian relief and longer-term efforts to improve the capacity of local healthcare providers.Why the donation comes amid global aid cutsThe $50 million gift comes at a time when reductions in international aid funding have disrupted healthcare programmes in several countries.According to the Associated Press, Americares has lost support for projects including a maternal-care programme in Tanzania. Medical clinics in Colombia serving Venezuelan migrants also closed after private funders had supported them for several months.The funding pressures have affected a wider range of humanitarian services, including maternal and child healthcare, HIV treatment and prevention, and medical assistance for vulnerable populations.Americares had previously received some funding from the US government, which accounted for approximately 10% of its funding before recent aid cuts, the Associated Press reported. The organisation has since continued its work through a mix of individual donors, corporations and private foundations.The new donation will provide additional resources for its healthcare expansion plans while strengthening its ability to sustain programmes over time.Half the donation will strengthen Americares' endowmentOne of the defining features of the gift is the decision to allocate $25 million to Americares' endowment rather than direct healthcare expansion.An endowment is a pool of financial assets intended to support an organisation over the long term. It can help generate income for future activities and reduce dependence on short-term grants or individual funding commitments.For a humanitarian organisation, financial stability can be particularly important because healthcare programmes require consistent supplies, staffing and support. Interruptions in funding can affect a clinic's ability to maintain services or provide patients with essential medicines.By increasing its endowment, Americares intends to strengthen its financial resilience and protect its capacity to deliver healthcare in the future. The remaining $25 million will support the expansion of its healthcare work, creating a balance between immediate programme needs and long-term sustainability.Anonymous family has supported Americares for 30 yearsAmericares said the donation came from a philanthropic Connecticut family that has supported the organisation for approximately three decades. The family has chosen not to disclose its identity publicly.Christine Squires, president and CEO of Americares, said the family understood the challenges facing global health and wanted to do more in response to the growing needs.The organisation described the contribution as a significant investment in its five-year strategic plan, which includes expanding its network of local healthcare partners, improving access to medicines and strengthening emergency-response capabilities.Americares also hopes the record-breaking gift will encourage other philanthropists to support humanitarian healthcare initiatives as organisations face mounting pressure to maintain essential services.You use AI every day.
